messages.author: b9400d58a0bfce63
messages.subject: MIMS as an external function
parts:
Hi,

As has been discussed previously, GGIR does not currently have a way to automatically calculate MIMS units directly within a normal GGIR function call. As such, it seemed like a sensible temporary solution to set up the MIMSunit package function as an external function provided to GGIR. The process of doing this is straightforward thanks to great documentation and examples on the github page (thanks Vincent and others!).

To facilitate this as an easily accessible path for other users who might be interested in doing the same such that MIMS can be calculated with some standardization to other metrics (e.g., the handling of nonwear time for ENMO calculations), I put together a very simple Rmarkdown file (see attached html) describing the process. In testing so far it seems to provide reasonable estimates.

Before putting this out there as an Rpub document that others might use, I am hoping to check whether there is anything obviously egregious that makes the external function approach invalid for MIMS regarding the way data are internally handled. If so I would really like to avoid leading others astray! Caveats about speed based on previous conversations are acknowledged. Any other thoughts or suggestions also appreciated.

Thank you for your time and help,
Tom

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MIMS as an external function
parts:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for sharing, I guess this is helpful for some.
Here a my comments:

Currently, this procedure produces values that are not exactly the same as those produced by running the...

This paragraph invalidates your approach because a new implementation that it is not consistent with the original is problematic in research. Instead, turn off auto-calibration (do.cal = FALSE) and imputation (do.imp=FALSE) and make sure your reference 5 seconds estimates are just like GGIR aligned with the start of a minute. The resulting values should be identical. If not, then I think you cannot recommend this approach to the research community, because there are inconsistencies without explanation. Instead of promoting the method it would then be best to invest the energy in researching the differences.

It is also important to note that the issue of calculating MIMS from within GGIR is not new, and has previously received attention from developers of both groups (s

I would like to propose removing the last paragraph and replacing it with a call for researchers to find funding to speed up the MIMSunit package, because that is ultimately the best solution for the community. It allows us to embed MIMSunit as a dependency of GGIR such that we no longer need this external function solution and it makes it easier for anyone using R to work with MIMSunit. The discussion I had with the MIMSunit was just a discussion and I would be really worried if researchers started using these code snippets I shared without doing further research first. I am concerned that it will lead to unnecessary methodological inconsistencies.

Best,

Vincent

messages.author: b9400d58a0bfce63
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MIMS as an external function
parts:
Hi Vincent,

My sincere thank you for your thoughtful comments. Of course that's a great idea to set do.cal and do.imp = FALSE, I don't know why that didn't occur to me. When doing so, the MIMS output is nearly identical to the original but with some very minor differences. In attempting to dig deeply into this, I can see with a breakpoint within my external function that the raw acceleration values being used in the external function are not quite the same as those that are used when reading the data in directly with GGIRread (readAxivity() ). These differences in the acceleration data appear to account for the differences that I am seeing in the final products. 

This surprised me given that imputation and auto-calibration should be disabled. So I figured that this could be due to some other potential candidate settings, which I configured as follows:
"GGIR(...,
nonWearEdgeCorrection = F,
ignorenonwear=F,
spherecrit=0,
interpolationType=1,
frequency_tol=0.1,
backup.cal.coef = "redo")"

As I would have originally expected, none of these parameters made a difference: the acceleration values used at the time of the external function are still not the same at relevant timepoints as those that come from a readAxivity() of the raw .cwa file.

My next suspicion was that the difference was coming from the resampling procedure that occurs here in the GGIR codebase: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/19a8c42009a8315f89c3f2a8956619d7d3400648/R/g.readaccfile.R#L248
However, after a thorough inspection, the resampling procedure also does not appear to account for any of the differences in the acceleration data that I am noting at the time of external function application.

So, I am wondering if you could point me towards any other place in GGIR that would transform the acceleration data prior to application of an external function? I have searched elsewhere in the list of parameters and traced the processing steps in the code base for Axivity files, but haven't been able to find any other good candidates.

Finally, regarding your last point, I agree wholeheartedly and will change the document accordingly. As a side note, my own tweaks to speed up mims_unit without changing outcomes at all (mainly through improved vectorization) have only managed to reduce runtimes by a meager ~3%... my suspicion is that in order to keep the entire original MIMS algorithm, the best bet may be to move computationally intensive parts to C++ via Rcpp. Something I hope to delve into in the future, though perhaps a fool's errand?

Thank you,
Tom

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MIMS as an external function
parts:
To close out this issue in case others encounter something similar:

I am now able to perfectly reproduce mims_unit() outcomes when running as an external function through GGIR. The differences I previously observed stemmed from a non-obvious source, the setup of the timestamp sequence from a rounded starttime: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/19a8c42009a8315f89c3f2a8956619d7d3400648/R/applyExtFunction.R#L53

Notably, GGIR versus the use of readAxivity() output fed directly into mims_unit() were handling a boundary point differently occuring right near the starttime, leading to some non-alignment in binning between the two approaches (e.g., a numeric value with something like 1653961499.999197959).

So, I am wondering if you could point me towards any other place in GGIR that would transform the acceleration data prior to application of an external function? I have searched elsewhere in the list of parameters and traced the processing steps in the code base for Axivity files, but haven't been able to find any other good candidates.

Finally, regarding your last point, I agree wholeheartedly and will change the document accordingly.
